haiku-low.q1: The network is reachable again, the app comes to the foreground, or a 60-second timer fires while online.
haiku-low.q2: Upload first. Download starts only after all upload batches succeed.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it. It compares the change's base_version with the note's current version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: The first phone's body becomes N at version 4. The second phone's body is kept in a new conflict note titled "T (conflict)" at version 1.
haiku-low.q5: One change with the latest body, keeping the first base_version and change_id from the outbox row.
haiku-low.q6: The server records each change_id and its result in processed, in the same transaction. A retry returns the stored result and writes nothing.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, in sync_state(cursor). It is updated in the same local transaction that applies the downloaded entries.
haiku-low.q8: The cursor did not move past unapplied entries, so the phone refetches from the old cursor. Re-applying is harmless and nothing is skipped.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict response carries the server's current note state, and the phone overwrites title, body and server_version with it. Nothing notifies the user; the conflict note arrives on download.
haiku-low.q10: After the server's response for it arrives (applied or conflict), the phone deletes its outbox row in one local transaction.
haiku-low.q11: The download entry is skipped and the local edit is kept. It uploads later with its old base version, conflicts, and the response brings the current server state.
haiku-low.q12: It is held in next_body on the same outbox row, and body is untouched. When the ack arrives, it is queued as a new change with a new change_id.

sonnet.q1: Three triggers: the phone regains its network connection (OS reports reachable), the app comes to the foreground, and a 60-second timer while online. A trigger during a running sync sets a flag and runs one more sync afterwards.
sonnet.q2: Upload first (all batches must succeed), then download.
sonnet.q3: The server detects it. It compares the change's base_version with the note's current server version; a mismatch is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first-arriving write wins: note N is accepted and its version goes up by 1 (e.g. 3 to 4), with A's body. The second phone's change conflicts, so the server creates a new conflict note (title plus ' (conflict)', version 1) holding the losing body, and N is unchanged by it. The change log gets entries for both, and processed rows store each result.
sonnet.q5: One change per note: later edits overwrite the body of the same outbox row, keeping the same change_id and base_version. So it sends a single change with the full latest body (no diffs).
sonnet.q6: Each change has a change_id (UUID). The server's processed table stores the result per change_id, written in the same transaction as the write. On a retry with a known change_id, the server returns the stored result and writes nothing. The retry resends the same body and change_id.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's local SQLite sync_state table as the cursor (the last seq fully applied). It is updated in the same local transaction that applies a downloaded page's entries, set to the last seq in the page.
sonnet.q8: The cursor only moves in the same transaction as the applied entries, so it stays at the old value. The next sync refetches from the old cursor. The version check (skip if entry.version <= server_version) makes re-applying harmless, and no entries are skipped.
sonnet.q9: The upload response says conflict and carries N's current server state (version, title, body). The phone applies it like a download entry: overwrites title and body and sets server_version, under the same version check, and deletes the outbox row. The losing edit now lives only in the conflict note, which reaches the phone through the next download. The user is not notified (open point).
sonnet.q10: When the server's response for that change arrives (applied or conflict). The phone handles each result in one local transaction and deletes the outbox row. If the request fails, the row stays (sent=1) and is resent.
sonnet.q11: If the note has an outbox row, the download skips that entry (the cursor still moves past it). The local edit is kept and later uploads with its old base version, so it conflicts. The conflict response brings the current server state, so the skipped body is not missed.
sonnet.q12: The edit goes into next_body on the same outbox row, and body is never touched, so a retry resends the same body under the same change_id. When the ack arrives, the phone queues next_body as a new change with a new change_id and sets notes.body to it. Its base_version is v on applied(v), or the version from the response's current state on conflict.
